title: 第三节为什么一个原因总是必然的

content.value:
首先从关于原因的必然性这第一个问题开始探究。哲学中有一条一般公理：所有开始存在的东西必定有一个存在的原因。
人们在所有推理中都既不举出证明也不要求证明，而通常把这一点看做是理所当然的。这是被假定为建立在直觉之上的那些公理之一，尽管人们可能会在口头上否定这个公理，但在心中却不可能真的怀疑它。但是，如果我们根据上述的知识观念来考察这个公理，我们将会发现，在这个公理中没有这类直觉确定性的任何迹象；相反，我们将会发现这个公理与那类信念的本性完全不相符合。
所有确定性都是来自于观念的比较、以及对那些只要各观念保持同一就总是不变的关系的发现。这些关系就是类似关系、量和数的比例、任何性质的程度和对立关系，其中没有一种关系包含在下述命题之中：凡是有开始存在的事物也都有一个存在的原因。因此，这个命题就不是直觉地确定的。至少，任何人如果断定这个命题是直觉确定的话，他就必须否认这些关系是唯一可靠无误的关系，而且必须发现包含在这种关系中的其他某种同类的关系；对于这一点，我们将有足够的时间加以考察。
但是，这里有一个论证，可以立刻就证明上述命题既没有直
—161一

proposition is neither intuitively nor demonstrably certain. We can
never demonstrate the necessity of a cause to every new existence, or
new modification of existence, without shewing at the same time the
impossibility there is, that any thing can ever begin to exist without
some productive principle; and where the latter proposition cannot be
prov' d, we must despair of ever being able to prove the former. Now
that the latter proposition is utterly incapable of a demonstrative proof,
we may satisfy ourselves by considering, that as all distinct ideas are
separable from each other, and as the ideas of cause and effect are
evidently distinct,’twill be easy for us to conceive any object to be
non-existent this moment, and existent the next, without conjoining to
it the distinct idea of a cause or productive principle. The separation,
therefore, of the idea of a cause from that of a beginning of existence,
is plainly possible for the imagination; and consequently the actual
separation of these objects is so far possible, that it implies no contra-
diction nor absurdity; and is therefore incapable of being refuted by
any reasoning from mere ideas; without which'tis impossible to dem-
onstrate the necessity of a cause.
Accordingly we shall find upon examination, that every
demonstration, which has been produc′ d for the necessity of a
cause, is fallacious and sophistical. All the points of time and
place ①, say some philosophers, in which we can suppose any
object to begin to exist, are in themselves equal; and unless
there be some cause, which is peculiar to one time and to one
place, and which by that means determines and fixes the exist-
ence, it must remain in etermal suspence; and the object can never
begin to be, for want of something to fix its beginning. But I ask; Is
there any more difficulty in supposing the time and place to be fix′ d
without a cause, than to suppose the existence to be determin’d in that

觉的确定性，也没有论证的确定性。如果我们不表明，要是没有某种产生原理，任何东西决不能并始存在，那么，我们同时也就永远不能证明每一个新的存在或存在的每一个新的变形都有一个原因的必然性；如果后一个命题不能得到证明，那么我们对证明前一个命题就会没有希望。既然后一个命题是绝对不可能具有论证性的证明，那么，我们只有考虑下面这一点就可以满足了，这就是：既然所有个别的观念都是可以彼此分离的，而原因和结果的观念又显然是个别的，所以我们很容易就设想一个对象在这一麟间是不存在的，在下一个瞬间则是存在的，而不必对它加上一个个别的原因观念或产生原理的观念。因此，对想象来说，原因的观念和存在开始的观念的分离显然是可能的；其结果是，这些对象的实际分离，就其不包含矛盾、也不包含谬误来说，是完全可能的。因此这种分离就不可能被那些仅仅是根据观念的任何推理所驳倒。而如果驳不倒这一点，我们便不可能证明一个原因的必然性。
因此，在考察的基础上我们将发现，对原因的必然性所提出的每一个论证都是谬误的、诡群的。一些哲学家说：我们能够假设某一对象在其中开始存在的时间和空间的所有点，本身都是相等的；除非有某种原因为一个时间和一个地点所特有，并且通过那种方式决定和确定这种存在，这种存在就必定永远处于未定状态，而这个对象由于缺乏某种东西确定它的并始，也就永远不能开始存在。但是，我要问，假定时间和地点没有原因就可以被确定，就要比假定以那种方式确定的那个存在有更多的困难吗？在
①霍布斯先生。

manner ? The first question that occurs on this subject is always,
whether the object shall exist or not: The next,when and where it
shall begin to exist. If the removal of a cause be intuitively absurd in
the one case, it must be so in the other : And if that absurdity be not
clear without a proof in the one case, it will equally require one in the
other. The absurdity, then， of the one supposition can never be a
proof of that of the other; since they are both upon the same footing,
and must stand or fall by the same reasoning.
The second argument, which I find us′ d on this head, labours
under an equal difficulty. Every thing,' tis said, must have a cause ;
for if any thing wanted a cause, it wou' d produce itself; that is, exist
before it existed; which is impossible. But this reasoning is plainly
unconclusive; because it supposes, that in our denial of a cause we
still grant what we expressly deny，viz.that there must be a cause；
which therefore is taken to be the object itself; and zhat, no doubt, is
an evident contradiction. But to say that any thing is produc'd, or to
express myself more properly, comes into existence, without a cause,
is not to affirm, that’ tis itself its own cause; but on the contrary in
excluding all external causes, excludes a fortiori the thing itself which
is created. An object, that exists absolutely without any cause, cer-
tainly is not its own cause; and when you assert, that the one follows
from the other, you suppose the very point in question, and take it for
granted, that’ tis utterly impossible any thing can ever begin to exist
without a cause, but that upon the exclusion of one productive princi-
ple, we must still have recourse to another.
①Dr. Clarke and others

这个题目上出现的第一个问题总是：那个对象是否将要存在？其次使是，它将在什么时间、什么地点并始存在？如果在一种情况下除去原因在直觉上就是荒谬的，在另一种情况下也必定是如此的。如果在一种情况下不经一个证明便不能使得那个谬误清晰可见，在另一种情况下也就同时需要一个证明。因此，一个假定的谬误绝不能成为另一个假定的谬误的证据，因为它们都是建立在同一个立足点上，并且必然会因同样的推理而成立或不成立。
我发现人们对这个题目所用的第二个论证，也为相同的困难所苦恼。人们会说，每一事物都必定会有一个原因，因为如果某一事物缺乏一个原因，那么它就是自已将自己产生出来的，也即是说，在它存在之前它就已经存在了，而这是不可能的。不过，
这种推理显然是没有确定性的，因为它假定，在对一个原因加以否定的时候，我们仍然承认了我们明白地否认过的事情，即必须有一个原因，这个原因因此就被看作是对象本身；这无疑是一个明显的矛盾。但是，说某一事物没有原因就被产生出来，或者更恰当地说，就开始存在了，这并不是去断言它是它自身的原因；正相反，排除了一切外在的原因，就更加排除了被创造出来的那个事物本身。一个没有任何原因就绝对存在的对象，当然不是它自身的原因；而当你断言一个对象是从另一个对象中产生出来时，
你恰好是在假定一个有争议的论点，并且把任何事物没有一个原因就绝对不能存在视为理所当然。但是，在排除了一个产生原理之后，我们仍然必须求助于另外一条原理。
①克拉克博士和其他人。
一165

'Tis exactly the same case with the third argument, which has
been employ'd to demonstrate the necessity of a cause.Whatever is
produc′d without any cause, is produc′ d by nothing; or in other
words, has nothing for its cause. But nothing can never be a cause,
no more than it can be something, or equal to two right angles. By the
same intuition, that we perceive nothing not to be equal to two right
angles, or not to be something, we perceive, that it can never be a
cause; and consequently must perceive, that every object has a real
cause of its existence.
I believe it will not be necessary to employ many words in she-
wing the weakness of this argument, after what I have said of the fore-
going. They are all of them founded on the same fallacy, and are de-
riv'd from the same turn of thought. ‘Tis sufficient only to observe,
that when we exclude all causes we really do exclude them, and nei-
ther suppose nothing nor the object itself to be the causes of the exist-
ence; and consequently can draw no argument from the absurdity of
these suppositions to prove the absurdity of that exclusion. If every
thing, must have a cause , it follows, that upon the exclusion of other
causes we must accept of the object itself or of nothing as causes.
But'tis the very point in question, whether every thing must have a
cause or not; and therefore, according to all just reasoning, it ought
never to be taken for granted.
They are still more frivolous, who say, that every effect must have
a cause, because’tis imply′ d in the very idea of effect. Every effect
necessarily pre-supposes a cause; effect being a relative term, of which
cause is the correlative. But this does not prove , that every being must
be preceded by a cause; no more than it follows, because every hus-
band must have a wife, that therefore every man must be marry ' d.
①Mr.Locke.
166一

用来证明原因的必然性的第三个论证也完全是同样的情形。没有任何原因就被产生出来的所有东西，都是从“无”产生出来的，或者换句话说，它以无为其原因。但是，正如它不能成为某物，或者不能等于两个直角一样，无永不可能成为一个原因。我们通过直觉发现，“无”不等于两个直角，或者不是某个东西；通过同样的直觉，我们也可以发现它决不能成为一个原因。因此，我们必定会发现，每一个对象都有其存在的真实原因。
我相信，在我论述了前面两种论证之后，无须多费口舌就可以表明这个论证的弱点。它们全都是建立在同样的谬误上面，并且都是来自于同样的思路。仅仅对这一点加以陈述就够了，即当我们排除一切原因的时候，我们就真正地把它们排除了，我们既不假定“无”是存在的原因，也不假定对象本身是存在的原因。因此，不能根据从这些假定的荒谬性中推出的论证去证明那种排除是荒谬的。如果每一事物必定有一个原因，那么在排除了其他的原因以后，我们就必须承认对象自身或者无是原因。但是，争论的焦点正是在于是否每一事物都必定会有一个原因；因此，依照一切正确的推理，我们绝不应该把这一点视为是理所当然的。
还有一些人说，每一个结果必然会有一个原因，因为原因就蕴含在结果的观念中，这样的人更是轻率的。每一个结果必定会以一个原因作为前提，因为结果是一个相对的名词，而原因则是它的相关项目。但是，这并不能证明每一个存在必定会以一个原因为前提，正如我们不能因为每一个丈夫必然有一个妻子，因而就推论说每一个男人必定都是已婚的一样。这个问题的正确

The true state of the question is,whether every object, which begins
to exist, must owe its existence to a cause; and this I assert neither to
be intuitively nor demonstratively certain, and hope to have prov′ d it
sufficiently by the foregoing arguments,
Since it is not from knowledge or any scientific reasoning, that
we derive the opinion of the necessity of a cause to every new produc-
tion, that opinion must necessarily arise from observation and experi-
ence. The next question, then, shou' d naturally be, how experience
gitves rise to such α principle? But as I find it will be more convenient
to sink this question in the following, Why we conclude, that such par-
ticular causes must necessarily have such particular effects，and why we
form an inference from one to another ? we shall make that the subject
of our future enquiry. ′Twill, perhaps, be found in the end, that the
same answer will serve for both questions.
SECTION IV. Of The Component Parts Of Our
Reasonings Concerning Cause And Effect.
Tho' the mind in its reasonings from causes or effects carries its
view beyond those objects, which it sees or remembers, it must never
lose sight of them entirely, nor reason merely upon its own ideas,
without some mixture of impressions, or at least of ideas of the memo-
ry, which are equivalent to impressions. When we infer effects from
causes, we must establish the existence of these causes; which we
have only two ways of doing, either by an immediate perception of our
memory or senses, or by an inference from other causes; which cau-
ses again we must ascertain in the same manner, either by a present
impression, or by an inference from their causes, and so on, till we
arrive at some object, which we see or remember. ’ Tis impossible

陈述是：是否每一个开始存在的对象都必须把它的存在归因于一个原因。我已经断言，这一点既没有直觉的确定性，也没有论证的确定性，而且我希望通过前面的论证已经充分证明了这一点。
既然我们不是由知识或任何科学推理得出这样的意见，也即每一个新的产物都必然有一个原因，那么这个意见就必然是源自于观察和经验。因此，接下来的问题就自然是，经验是如何产生出这样一条原理的呢？不过我发现，把这个问题放到下面这个问题中将更为方使，即我们为什么会断言如此特定的原因必定会有如此特殊的结果？我们为什么要形成因果互推的推断？我们将把这个题目留待以后进行研究。最后，我们或许会发现，同一个答复将可以解决这两个问题。
